# pupnp / FuzzIxml

pupnp's own fuzz target `FuzzIxml` ([source](source/FuzzIxml.c), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over pupnp (pupnp/pupnp at b46bc77a).

writes the input (10..5120 bytes) to /tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>, ixmlLoadDocumentEx parses it, ixmlPrintDocument serialises it, then frees; the printed text is not compared to anything.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against pupnp at commit b46bc77a.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- if a document parsed, ixmlPrintDocument must return a non-empty string, else CheckXML returns 1 (and LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput returns it); trivially true because ixmlPrintDocument always emits the <?xml version="1.0"?> prolog (ixml/src/ixml.c:404), so only an allocation failure could make it NULL ([lines 23-27](source/FuzzIxml.c#L23-L27)): returns only; not confirmed in the binary.

The harness turns some inputs away by returning a value other than 0 or -1, which the driver reports as status 78, so its halts statements allow 78 as well:
- An input shorter than 10 bytes or longer than 5120 is returned 1 without being parsed ([lines 41-43](source/FuzzIxml.c#L41-L43)).
- An input ixmlLoadDocumentEx does not parse is returned its nonzero IXML error code ([lines 18-21](source/FuzzIxml.c#L18-L21)).

The status does not say which line returned, so a failure of a check above that reports it by returning (FuzzIxml.c:23-27) also exits with status 78, and these statements allow it.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch pupnp` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `FuzzIxml.plain` | 67,416 | `c205148fe52384962320d68959925cb0a712dd46394a3360e2ef0083c0ddd389` |
| ubsan | `FuzzIxml.ubsan` | 69,712 | `e26c655c2dd8f741b048c13f7109dd3bf16da13e2e9e70d95eb893ebd1db41b7` |
| asan | `FuzzIxml.asan` | 618,232 | `e1f0d4758038e48a10ba670236f313a50f766ba09a1eed419cd0beed62a2fee3` |
| asan-ubsan | `FuzzIxml.asan-ubsan` | 620,504 | `ae232c534fcf810bf9f8aae1fd52de1334eed3eba7a668bb8f2bc8bd139e24ab` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
